_why: Fixtures for scripts/short-circuit-check.mjs, held here rather than inline because that scanner reads scripts/*.mjs and would otherwise flag its own test data. Kept beside the other deliberately-wrong fixtures in this directory. Every `bad` entry is a REAL line, copied from the commit that fixed it.
bad: run: () => ok('npm run check') && ok('npm run check:hard') },
good: run: () => all('npm run check', 'npm run check:hard') },

blind.why: a glob string that opens a block comment ('/**') and a later one that closes it ('**/*.'); the shape of check-ignore-parity.mjs. The old stripper paired the two across the line between them
a line comment that holds a /* (src/*.js) and a doc comment that closes later; the shape of history-check.mjs. The old stripper read the line comment's /* as a block comment's opener
a // inside a string, on the line of the offence. The old per-line rule skipped only '://' and cut the line there
a multi-line block comment before the offence. The old stripper deleted it, newlines included, so every later line number came out too low

_blind_notes: Each entry holds ONE offence, on `line` (1-based). `src` is the whole file text, so a comment's opener and closer can be a few lines apart. The first three were missed by the old stripper (measured 2026-11-05: 81 of 16,281 positions in 10 scripts, by planting this offence at every statement start); the fourth was seen on the wrong line.

_good_notes.survived: A PRECONDITION, not a second measurement. `built` is the result of `npm run build`; if the build failed, running the expect would measure a broken tree rather than the mutation. Short-circuiting is correct here, and a rule that flagged it would train the reader to ignore the rule.
